### Observed differences

- Activity A01 appears only in the later window: it is absent from all 200 earlier traces and occurs exactly once in each of the 200 later traces (participation 0 → 100 in 100 cases, mean one execution per case) [OCC001].
- In the earlier window the process ended with A16, which occupied the final position of every trace (relative position 1.0 with no spread) and had no observed outgoing transitions. In the later window A16 sits second to last (mean relative position about 0.92) and all of its roughly 200 observed outgoing transitions lead to A01, which itself always occupies the final position [POS016, DIR009, POS001, REL015].
- A01 now co-occurs with the other activities in essentially every case: A04, A13 and A16 run before A01 in 100 of 100 later traces, and the activities present in every trace (A02, A09, A11, A14) co-occur with A01 in all traces [REL003, REL012, REL015, REL001, REL008, REL010, REL013].
- The relative positions of nearly all long-standing activities shifted slightly earlier, by about the amount expected when one event is appended at the end of each trace (for example A13 from about 0.91 to 0.85, A04 from 0.83 to 0.77, A11 from 0.48 to 0.46) [POS004, POS011, POS013, POS014, POS016].
- Beyond this, behaviour is broadly stable: participation and repetition of the other activities changed little (largest residual: A10, about 1.9 → 2.1 executions per trace, in about 67 → 64 of 100 traces), with minor routing shifts (A08 sends about 16 of 100 outgoing transitions to A02 in the later window versus about 10 of 100 earlier; A03's split between A05 and A06 moved from about 47/53 to 52/48) and somewhat less frequent precedence of A10 before A13/A16 (about 24 → 16 of 100 cases) [OCC002, OCC009, DIR004, DIR002, REL092, REL095].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that a new activity, A01, was appended as the final step of the process: in the later window every case contains A01 exactly once, at the end of the trace, immediately after A16, whereas in the earlier window every case ended with A16 and A01 never appeared. The support is direct and consistent across indicator families — occurrence (0 → 100% participation, once per case), position (A01 last in every later trace; A16 moving from last to second-to-last), successor evidence (the new A16 → A01 transition carries all of A16's outgoing transitions), and pairwise relations (A04, A13 and A16 always precede A01; A01 co-occurs with every ubiquitous activity). Each of these items shows a reference strength of about 0.995, exceeded by essentially none of the 200 random re-splits, and the slight backward shift of the other activities' relative positions matches the mechanical effect of appending one event rather than indicating separate moves [OCC001, POS001, POS016, DIR009, REL003, REL012, REL015, REL008, POS004, POS013].

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a genuinely new activity from a relabelling or split of the previous final step, since it shows only that A16 is now followed by A01 in every case and the activity codes are anonymous [DIR009, REL015]. The evidence set also provides no screening baseline, so the flagged-item count cannot be compared with the number expected by chance; the judgement rests on the directness and mutual consistency of the A01 items. The small routing and ordering shifts reported below are not explained by the appended activity and could equally be sampling variation between the windows [DIR004, DIR002, OCC009].

Other differences:
- A08 routes relatively more often to A02: about 10 of 100 of its outgoing transitions before, about 16 of 100 after (A09 falling from about 90 to 84) [DIR004].
- A03's choice between successors A05 and A06 tilted toward A05 (about 47/53 → 52/48) [DIR002].
- A10 executes slightly more often per trace (about 1.9 → 2.1) but in slightly fewer traces, and precedes A13 or A16 somewhat less often than before [OCC009, REL092, REL095].
- Several lag distributions show marginal redistributions, some resting on very few observations (for example A10 → A09 with 8 versus 14 observations, A09 → A09 with 2 versus 1) [LAG055, LAG046].
